requirements.spec: Every function exported through index.js must have a null-guard as its first statement
requirements.expected_artifact: Each exported function body begins with `if (arg == null) throw new TypeError(...)`
requirements.evidence: capitalize: `if (s == null) throw new TypeError('capitalize: argument is required');` is line 2 (first statement). slugify: same pattern line 5. clamp: `if (n == null) throw new TypeError('clamp: argument is required');` line 2. sum: same pattern line 5. isoDay: `if (dt == null) throw new TypeError('isoDay: argument is required');` line 2. checksum: `if (buf == null) throw new TypeError('checksum: argument is required');` line 3.

requirements.spec: The guard must throw new TypeError('<functionName>: argument is required')
requirements.expected_artifact: Exact error constructor and message format match spec
requirements.evidence: All 6 functions use `throw new TypeError('<functionName>: argument is required')` with exact matching function names in the message

requirements.spec: The guard must fire if the first argument is null OR undefined
requirements.expected_artifact: Guard uses loose equality `== null` or explicit double check
requirements.verification_run: Inspected guard conditions in all files
requirements.evidence: All guards use `== null` which in JavaScript covers both null and undefined

requirements.spec: The guard must execute before anything else
requirements.expected_artifact: Guard is the very first statement inside each function body
requirements.evidence: In every function, the null-guard is the first executable line, no preceding assignments, calls, or logic
